title: How Does GPS Know Your Exact Location? 🛰️
description: Your phone never sends anything to satellites! It just listens to the time and does some smart math. And the surprise: without Einstein's theory, GPS would miss by miles every single day!

scenes.say: You open the map, and within seconds your phone knows your exact location. So how does GPS actually work?

scenes.label: About 31 satellites
scenes.say: About thirty-one satellites orbit twenty thousand kilometers up, constantly broadcasting the exact time and their location.

scenes.caption: Your phone only receives
scenes.say: Your phone never sends anything to the satellites. It only listens to their signals and calculates how long they took to arrive.
From the signal time, it finds the distance to each satellite. With at least four satellites, their ranges intersect at one single point, which is your location.
And the twist? Satellite clocks tick thirty-eight microseconds faster every day due to Einstein's relativity. Without correcting this, GPS would be off by ten kilometers daily.
